# Wizz.js

> Wizz.js is a zero-dependency, full-stack JavaScript framework. Single-file `.wizz` components compile ahead of time to plain DOM creation/update code and statically scoped CSS. Pages server-render by default and hydrate in the browser, with no Virtual DOM, no npm runtime packages, and built-in server API routes. Current version: compiler 1.17.1, syntax 1.4.2, output 1.8.3.

Wizz.js is not React, Vue, or Svelte, and most idioms from those frameworks fail to compile. Before writing a `.wizz` file, read [the full reference](/llms-full.txt). The rules that trip agents up most:

- A template has exactly one native root element.
- `{...}` accepts only identifiers, member access (`a.b.c`), string and integer literals, `+ - * /` with parentheses, and strict equality (`a === "b"`). No function calls, ternaries, `!`, `!==`, `<`/`>`, or `&&`/`||`: compute values in `<script>` and reference them by name.
- Dynamic attributes must be unquoted: `class={cardClass}` or `class={"card " + state}`. A quoted value such as `class="card {state}"` renders the braces literally. Dynamic attributes other than `value`/`checked`/`disabled` are stringified and never removed, so `hidden={false}` still hides. There is no `bind:`.
- Components are self-closing tags inside a native element: no children, no slots, and no `on:` directives on component tags (pass callback props).
- `{#each}` sits inside a native element, has one native root element per row, and its body may not contain components, `on:` directives, or nested `{#if}`/`{#each}`. Delegate events from the parent.
- Top-level `let` is reactive; update by reassignment (`items = [...items, x]`), not mutation (`items.push(x)`).
- `{#if}` picks its branch once at mount, and there is no `{:else if}`. Toggle interactive visibility with a bound class.
- Assignments in inline `on:` handlers update the DOM (`on:input={(e) => name = e.target.value}`). Releases before 1.17.1 did not track them; upgrade with `wizz update`.
- The Wizz MCP server's `project_overview` and `language_contract` tools return these limits as a table with working patterns (1.17.1+).
- `onMount`, `onDestroy`, and `persist` are compiler globals: call them without importing. Read `window`/`document` only inside `onMount`.

## Getting started

- [Installation & Setup](/docs/getting-started): Install the CLI, scaffold a project, project layout, first component, dev server, production build, editor setup.

## Core concepts

- [Components & Templating](/docs/components): Component anatomy, the template expression grammar, dynamic attributes, props, composition, scoped styles, `<wizz:head>`, lifecycle, and the rules the compiler enforces.
- [State & Reactivity](/docs/reactivity): Reactive `let`, microtask batching, which mutations are tracked, events, keyed and keyless `{#each}`, `{#if}`, `persist()`, derived-value and cleanup patterns.
- [Routing & Navigation](/docs/routing): File-system routes, the route manifest, the client router, links, view transitions, query parameters, guards and redirects.
- [Server APIs & SSR](/docs/server): `src/server/api/*.js` handlers, the request context, return values, `.env.server` secrets, server rendering eligibility, deploying with the node adapter.

## Reference

- [API Reference](/docs/api): Script globals, template directives, generated module exports, compiler API, router, handler contract, and the full `WIZZ-P`/`WIZZ-G` diagnostic code catalog.
- [CLI](/docs/cli): `wizz init`, `dev`, `build` (`--json`, `--adapter node`), `mcp`, `update`, `install-vscode-extension`, `--version`.
- [MCP Server](/docs/mcp): The six tools `wizz mcp` exposes to AI agents, the recommended agent loop, and the security model.

## Optional

- [Architecture & Philosophy](/docs/architecture): Why zero dependencies and no Virtual DOM, the compiler pipeline, the update model, SSR and hydration internals, CSS delivery, versioning, security boundaries.
- [Live Examples](/docs/examples): Persisted counter, keyed todo list, parent-to-child props, lifecycle clock, server API call.
- [Source code](https://github.com/duncantidd/wizz.js): The Wizz.js repository, releases, and installer.
